domain_claim: Changing an Ask prompt changes the canonical digest
notes: Two WorkflowSource values differing ONLY in an Ask.prompt field must not collide. Kani can bounded-check for specific prompt pairs; proptest can exhaustively test randomized prompts.

domain_claim: Changing an Ask timeout changes the canonical digest
notes: Two WorkflowSource values differing ONLY in an Ask.timeout field must not collide. Cover both None vs Some and Some(v1) vs Some(v2) cases. Ensure timeout sentinel does not collide with actual timeout value bytes.

domain_claim: canonical_digest is deterministic: same input always produces same output
notes: Compile the same source twice, assert digest equality. Proptest: round-trip through canonical_digest with generated WorkflowSource values, verify consistency.

domain_claim: An Ask with empty prompt produces a well-defined digest distinct from non-empty prompts
notes: Verify that hasher.update(b"") produces a valid and distinct contribution. Kani can prove for arbitrary non-empty strings that the empty-string hash is distinct.

domain_claim: timeout: None and timeout: Some("") produce different digest contributions
notes: Verify sentinel b"no_timeout" does not collide with b"timeout" + b"". Kani can prove None and Some("") produce distinct hash states.

domain_claim: Both duplicate canonical_digest implementations produce identical output for identical sources
notes: After fix is applied to both copies, verify they produce the same digest for a representative set of sources including Ask primitives.

domain_claim: Set and Finish primitive digest behavior is unchanged after the Ask fix
notes: The fix only adds an Ask arm. Existing arms are unchanged. Regression test ensures Set/Finish digests are identical before and after the fix.

domain_claim: Ask field hashing order is deterministic: tag then prompt then timeout
model_boundary: vb_compile::mod_compile_lowering::part_05::digest_step_primitive — field update ordering within Ask arm
notes: The order of hasher.update() calls within the Ask arm determines the hash output. Kani can prove that the update sequence is always executed in the same order for the same input.

domain_claim: digest_step_primitive never panics, unwraps, or expects on any valid StepPrimitive::Ask variant
notes: All field accesses on prompt (String::as_bytes) and timeout (Option::match) are infallible. Kani can prove no panic paths exist. This is a Holzman Rust requirement.

domain_claim: digest_step_primitive has an explicit Ask match arm (no catch-all for Ask)
notes: Verified by code review and static analysis: the Ask variant is explicitly matched, not covered by the catch-all 'other' arm. This prevents future silent regression if Ask fields are added.
